feedback:
Approved. This is the only review round left in this iteration (remaining_budget shows one run, and no model actions remain for a revision), so a revise decision could not race. The candidate is the iteration 7 best (688.5) resubmitted unchanged: kp 2.8, kd 0.9, ki 0, base_speed 1.1, sensor_weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], line_loss 'last_direction', sensor_size 0.012, and the iteration 4 spread (x = -0.024 to 0.024 m at y = 0.04 m). Every field is inside its contract range. Iteration 7 is the only raced design that has finished the oval and s-bend 20 of 20, so this is the baseline to beat. I make no prediction of its performance on this race.

What the earlier evidence shows: the slalom has finished 0 of 20 in every iteration. Its max_error has stayed between 0.061 and 0.064 across base_speed (iteration 4), sensor spread (iteration 5), kd (iteration 6), kp (iteration 7) and sensor_size 0.016 (iteration 8, which also cut s-bend completion to 13 of 20 and scored 610.4). rms_error is low on every track, so the slalom losses are edge excursions, not poor average tracking.

For the next iteration, the Optimizer should change one untested lever at a time from this design, and only if the race shows the slalom still off track. Keep the oval and s-bend at 20 of 20 as the constraint. Revert to this design if a change drops either below that.
requested_changes: If slalom max_error is still at or above 0.06 with line_loss_events near 1, test a forward sensor offset: set geometry.sensor_positions y from 0.04 to 0.06 for all five sensors, keeping the iteration 7 x values and sensor_weights, because the y position has never been tested and gives more lead time on the tape.

Alternatively, or if the forward offset fails, test geometry.sensor_size 0.008 with the iteration 7 spread, since the 0.016 footprint hurt the s-bend (iteration 8, 13 of 20) and the smaller footprint is the remaining edge-sharpness test.

Keep geometry.sensor_positions x at -0.024 to 0.024 m and base_speed at 1.1. Iteration 5 widened the spread to ±0.03 m and cut the score from 555.0 to 513.3, so do not return to the wider array without new evidence.
